<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="מנחם אב_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919986_theRebbe_397" batchId="meluket-_D7_9E_D7_A0_D7_97_D7_9D_20_D7_90_D7_91_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919986_theRebbe_397__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the date and heading for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Wednesday,</t>
    <t s="2">the fifteenth of Av, 5735*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section questions the comparison between the joy of the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur, and why this teaching concludes Tractate Ta'anis.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">There were no better days for Israel than the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="1">and it is necessary to understand what is the reason for the similarity and the common denominator between the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur.</t>
    <t s="2">Also, it is necessary to understand that this statement</t>
    <t s="3">("There were no better days etc.")</t>
    <t s="4">is at the conclusion and seal</t>
    <t s="5">of Tractate Ta'anis,</t>
    <t s="6">and yet festivals are a matter of joy,</t>
    <t s="7">the opposite of the matter of fasting.</t>
    <t s="8">And especially, from the language "There were no better days for Israel than the fifteenth of Av etc." it is evident that the joy of the fifteenth of Av</t>
    <t s="9">(and Yom Kippur)</t>
    <t s="10">is greater than the joy of a festival, even though it is a positive commandment from the Torah,</t>
    <t s="11">"And you shall rejoice in your festival,"</t>
    <t s="12">and according to this, the connection of this matter to</t>
    <t s="13">(the conclusion and seal)</t>
    <t s="14">of Tractate Ta'anis specifically is even more difficult.</t>
    <t s="15">Now, the connection of the fifteenth of Av to the matter of fasting is also evident from the fact that it links</t>
    <t s="16">(in the Mishnah)</t>
    <t s="17">the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="18">for Yom Kippur is the only fast day from the Torah,</t>
    <t s="19">and this fast is unique and different from other fasts also in that the four fasts</t>
    <t s="20">(and also the fasts enumerated in Megillas Taanis,</t>
    <t s="21">and several of them are brought in the Tur)</t>
    <t s="22">will be turned into joy and gladness,</t>
    <t s="23">but this is not the case regarding the fast of Yom Kippur, which will remain even in the future.</t>
    <t s="24">And from this that it links</t>
    <t s="25">(in the Mishnah)</t>
    <t s="26">the fifteenth of Av with Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="27">it is evident</t>
    <t s="28">that the festival of the fifteenth of Av is related not only to the matter of fasting in Tractate Ta'anis</t>
    <t s="29">[therefore the statement "There were no better days for Israel than the fifteenth of Av" is at the conclusion and seal of Tractate Ta'anis],</t>
    <t s="30">but also to the fast of Yom Kippur.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the joy of the fifteenth of Av relates to the weakening of the sun's power, which parallels Yom Kippur's atonement through human service.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, the reason why the fifteenth of Av is a festival</t>
    <t s="1">[for superficially it is not understood,</t>
    <t s="2">and as the Gemara asks:</t>
    <t s="3">Granted, Yom Kippur, because it has forgiveness and pardon,</t>
    <t s="4">the day on which the latter tablets were given,</t>
    <t s="5">but the fifteenth of Av, what is it?],</t>
    <t s="6">is brought in the discourses</t>
    <t s="7">from the Pri Etz Chaim,</t>
    <t s="8">because then is the filling of the moon.</t>
    <t s="9">And it questions this in the discourses,</t>
    <t s="10">but every month has a fifteenth day</t>
    <t s="11">(when it is the filling of the moon),</t>
    <t s="12">and what is the superiority of the fifteenth of Av specifically,</t>
    <t s="13">and from what is said "There were no better days etc. like the fifteenth of Av" it implies that it is superior even to the fifteenth of Nissan</t>
    <t s="14">(Pesach)</t>
    <t s="15">and the fifteenth of Tishrei</t>
    <t s="16">(Sukkos).</t>
    <t s="17">Now, one of the reasons in the Gemara there</t>
    <t s="18">(for why the fifteenth of Av is a festival)</t>
    <t s="19">is,</t>
    <t s="20">because then the power of the sun weakened.</t>
    <t s="21">And it is not understood,</t>
    <t s="22">the weakening of the sun's power is a matter in the heavenly luminaries and does not pertain to man's affairs and actions</t>
    <t s="23">(like the other reasons in the Gemara there),</t>
    <t s="24">and if so, what is the festival when the sun's power weakened?</t>
    <t s="25">And although from this that the sun's power weakened</t>
    <t s="26">(even though it is a matter in the heavenly luminaries)</t>
    <t s="27">there are consequences regarding matters and actions on earth,</t>
    <t s="28">and as it states in the Gemara there, "and they would not cut wood for the arrangement etc.,"</t>
    <t s="29">nevertheless, from the language of the Gemara</t>
    <t s="30">("From the fifteenth of Av and onward the power of the sun weakened")</t>
    <t s="31">it implies that the festival</t>
    <t s="32">(and the joy)</t>
    <t s="33">of the fifteenth of Av is because of this very thing, that the power of the sun weakened</t>
    <t s="34">(and not only because of the consequences brought about by this),</t>
    <t s="35">and if so, it must be said,</t>
    <t s="36">that this too, that the power of the sun weakened, is related to the service of man.</t>
    <t s="37">For this is the equivalence of the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="38">that just as the atonement of Yom Kippur is accomplished through the service of man</t>
    <t s="39">[for although the essence of the day atones,</t>
    <t s="40">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="41">through the service of man the atonement is with greater strength and vigor.</t>
    <t s="42">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="43">even the atonement that comes from the essence of the day is specifically when a person fulfills</t>
    <t s="44">(holds himself)</t>
    <t s="45">the essence of the day,</t>
    <t s="46">for the excision of the day, Yom Kippur, does not atone],</t>
    <t s="47">so too it is regarding the weakening of the sun's power on the fifteenth of Av</t>
    <t s="48">[for even after it weakened etc. there is still the sun's power,</t>
    <t s="49">only that its power weakened],</t>
    <t s="50">it is a matter related to the service of man.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
